q.t: How many faces does a cuboid have?
q.e: Top and bottom, front and back, left and right.

q.t: How many edges does a cuboid have?
q.e: 4 lengths, 4 breadths and 4 heights.

q.t: How many vertices does a tetrahedron have?
q.e: Three on the triangular base and one at the top.

q.t: How many faces does a triangular prism have?
q.e: 2 triangular ends and 3 rectangular sides.

q.t: A polyhedron is a solid whose faces are all:
q.e: ‘Poly’ = many, ‘hedron’ = face: a solid bounded by flat polygon faces.

q.t: Is a cylinder a polyhedron?
o: No — it has a curved surface
Yes — it has two flat faces
q.e: Every face of a polyhedron must be a flat polygon; a cylinder’s side is curved.

q.t: How many vertices does a square pyramid have?
q.e: 4 corners of the base plus the apex.

q.t: What shape is each face of a cube?
o: Rectangle that is not a square
q.e: All edges of a cube are equal, so every face is a square.

q.t: How many vertices does a pentagonal prism have?
q.e: 5 on each of the two pentagonal ends.

q.t: How many faces does a hexagonal prism have?
q.e: 2 hexagonal ends plus 6 rectangular sides.

q.t: Euler’s formula for a polyhedron with F faces, V vertices and E edges is:
q.e: Check on a cube: 6 + 8 − 12 = 2. It holds for every convex polyhedron.

q.t: How many edges does a hexagonal prism have?
q.e: 6 on each end and 6 joining them: 3 × 6 = 18.

q.t: How many faces does an octagonal pyramid have?
q.e: 8 triangular faces plus the octagonal base.

q.t: A polyhedron has 6 faces and 12 edges. How many vertices does it have?
How many vertices does a pentagonal pyramid have?
q.e: 5 on the base plus the apex.

q.t: A polyhedron has 10 vertices and 15 edges. How many faces does it have?
q.e: F = 2 + E − V = 7 (a pentagonal prism).

q.t: A prism whose base has n sides has how many faces?
q.e: n side faces plus the 2 ends.

q.t: A pyramid whose base has n sides has how many edges?
q.e: n around the base and n slanting up to the apex.

q.t: A tetrahedron is another name for a:
q.e: ‘Tetra’ means four: it has four triangular faces.

q.t: In a regular polyhedron:
o: All faces are congruent regular polygons and the same number meet at each vertex
q.e: Regular means the same everywhere: identical regular faces and identical corners.

q.t: A polyhedron has 20 faces and 12 vertices. How many edges does it have?
A prism has 15 edges. How many faces does it have?
q.e: A prism has 3n edges, so n = 5. Faces = n + 2 = 7.

q.t: A pyramid has 7 vertices. How many edges does it have?
q.e: Vertices = n + 1, so n = 6. Edges = 2n = 12.

q.t: Is there a polyhedron with 4 faces, 4 vertices and 6 edges?
q.e: 4 + 4 − 6 = 2 ✓, and the tetrahedron is exactly this solid.

q.t: A polyhedron has 5 faces and 6 vertices. How many edges does it have?
q.e: E = 5 + 6 − 2 = 9 (a triangular prism).

q.t: How many regular polyhedra (Platonic solids) are there?
q.e: Tetrahedron, cube, octahedron, dodecahedron and icosahedron — only these five can be made.

q.t: An octahedron has 8 faces and 6 vertices. How many edges does it have?
A prism has 24 edges. How many vertices does it have?
q.e: 3n = 24 gives n = 8. Vertices = 2n = 16.

q.t: A pyramid has 9 faces. How many vertices does it have?
q.e: Faces = n + 1, so the base has 8 sides. Vertices = n + 1 = 9. (A pyramid always has as many vertices as faces.)

q.t: How many face diagonals does a cube have in all?
q.e: Each of the 6 square faces has 2 diagonals.

q.t: A prism has 30 edges. How many faces does it have?
q.e: 3n = 30, so the base has 10 sides. Faces = 10 + 2 = 12.

q.t: A pyramid has 20 edges. How many vertices does it have?
q.e: 2n = 20, so the base has 10 sides. Vertices = 10 + 1 = 11.

q.t: A dodecahedron has 12 faces, each a pentagon. How many edges does it have?
q.e: 12 pentagons have 60 sides, but each edge is shared by two faces: 60 ÷ 2 = 30.

q.t: A dodecahedron has 12 faces and 30 edges. How many vertices does it have?
An icosahedron has 20 triangular faces. How many vertices does it have?
How many space diagonals (through the inside) does a cube have?
q.e: Each one joins a vertex to the opposite vertex. 8 vertices make 4 such pairs.

q.t: Can a polyhedron have exactly 7 edges?
q.e: The smallest, a tetrahedron, has 6 edges; the next possible is 8 (square pyramid). 7 cannot be made.

q.t: One corner of a cube is sliced off with a flat cut. How many faces does the new solid have?
q.e: The 6 original faces remain (three of them trimmed), plus the new triangular cut face.

q.t: A football pattern has 12 pentagons and 20 hexagons as faces. How many edges does it have?
q.e: Total sides = 60 + 120 = 180, and each edge is shared by two faces: 90.

q.t: For a pentagonal prism, find F + V + E.
